0.0.n: さん makes this a polite way to address a group.

0.2.n: A standard daytime greeting; the final は is pronounced わ.

1.0.n: This is the first part of the organization name ひらがなネット.

1.1.n: This is the second part of the organization name ひらがなネット, not a separate reference to the internet.

1.2.n: Marks the organization where she teaches.

1.3.n: Refers to Japanese cuisine, which she teaches people to prepare.

1.4.m: Japanese cooking as the subject taught
1.4.n: Marks 和食 as what she teaches.

1.5.n: て-form of 教える plus いる describes her ongoing teaching work.

1.6.n: This is the speaker’s given name.

1.7.n: Politely ends her introduction; Japanese leaves out I here.

2.0.n: Refers to the current lesson or demonstration.

2.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic, setting the context for what follows.

2.2.n: A common name for shaped rice portions, often with fillings or seaweed.

2.3.m: rice balls as the thing made
2.3.n: Marks おにぎり as what they will make.

2.4.n: The polite form of 作る expresses a planned action here.

3.0.n: Usually means cooked rice or a meal; here it refers to rice being prepared.

3.1.n: Links ご飯 to 炊き方, specifying what will be cooked.

3.2.n: 炊く becomes 炊き before 方, which adds the sense of a method.

3.3.n: Marks the rice-cooking method as an additional thing she will show.

3.4.n: 紹介 plus します makes a polite verb; here she means showing viewers a method.

4.0.n: Signals a transition from the introduction to starting the activity.

4.2.n: Combines with に to describe doing an activity with someone else.

4.3.n: Turns 一緒 into a phrase describing how they will make the rice balls.

4.4.n: 作る with the polite ending ましょう invites viewers to join in.

0.tip: 皆さん politely addresses all the viewers at once.

1.lit: At Hiragana Net, Japanese cooking teaching Akiko am.
1.tip: 教えている comes before 明子 to describe her as the person who teaches Japanese cooking.

2.lit: This time, as for, rice balls will make.
2.tip: 作ります can describe a future action; here it announces what they will make.

3.lit: Rice’s cooking method also will introduce.
3.tip: Attach 方 to a verb’s stem to express how to do something.

4.tip: The polite ending ましょう invites someone to do something with you.
